scenes.head: Before go‑live, test the exceptions
scenes.say: What should you test before e-invoicing goes live? Start with the invoices that don't follow the normal path.

scenes.desc: In‑scope businesses with revenue of AED 50m or more.
scenes.src: Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025, Art. 5, as amended by Ministerial Resolution No. 66 of 2026 (mof.gov.ae). Checked 2 Nov 2026. Valorin is an independent advisory firm, not affiliated with the FTA or MoF.
scenes.say: For in-scope businesses with revenue of fifty million dirhams or more, e-invoicing must be implemented by the first of January, twenty twenty-seven.

Test credit notes against the original invoice. Agree who fixes a rejected or failed invoice, and how fast. Check buyer tax numbers and electronic addresses. And set up every company in the group, not only the main one.

captions.linkedin:
Before e-invoicing goes live, test the invoices that don't follow the normal path. That's where go-live problems usually start.

Under Ministerial Decision No. 244 of 2025, as amended by Ministerial Resolution No. 66 of 2026, in-scope businesses with revenue of AED 50m or more must implement e-invoicing by 1 January 2027 (mof.gov.ae, checked 2 Nov 2026).

Four e-invoicing implementation test cases we'd put on the list now:
• Credit notes, partial and full, linked to the original invoice
• Rejected or failed sends, with an owner and a fix time
• Buyer TRNs and electronic addresses in the customer master
• Every group company set up, not only the main one
